id_tips: 'ItSaul Summer': ItSaul Plants' everbearing red raspberry — fruits all summer long (catalog: All Summer Fruiting, 5' tall, 3' spacing).
Upright canes with leaves made of 3-5 toothed, deeply veined leaflets, whitish underneath.
Small white flowers followed by red raspberries that pull away from the core when ripe (leaving a hollow berry).
Everbearing (catalog): fruits all summer on the current year's canes.

care.light: Full sun: 6+ hours of direct sun. Fruit best with at least 6-8 hours of sun.
care.water: Keep evenly moist, especially while fruiting; mulch well.
care.soil: Rich, well-drained, slightly acid soil; avoid wet spots.

extra.label: Hardiness
extra.text: Hardy perennial shrub in Atlanta (red raspberries: about zones 4-8). Everbearing canes can be cut to the ground in late winter for one long summer-fall crop. It rambles like any raspberry, but ItSaul notes it can be kept in a container.

talk: Printed in bold in the catalog: a Saul Nurseries / ItSaul Plants exclusive introduction — a plant customers can't get just anywhere.
Saul's own ItSaul Plants introduction: “bears fruit all summer long” (ItSaul; catalog: All Summer Fruiting, everbearing).
Container-friendly: keep it in a big pot on the patio for easy picking and to stop it rambling.
Plant 3' apart (catalog) in a sunny row or big container.

id_tips: Low clumps of glossy leaves made of 3 toothed leaflets.
White five-petaled flowers with yellow centers, followed by red strawberries with seeds on the outside.
Spreads by long runners that root new plants (June-bearing and some everbearing types).
Catalog height 8-12", spacing 18".

care.light: Full sun: 6+ hours of direct sun..
care.water: Keep evenly moist, especially while fruiting; water at the base to prevent fruit rot.
care.soil: Rich, well-drained, slightly acid soil; great in raised beds, hanging baskets and strawberry jars.

extra.label: Hardiness
extra.text: Hardy perennial in Atlanta. Plant in fall or early spring. Mulch with pine straw to keep berries clean.

talk: June-bearers give one big crop in spring; everbearers/day-neutrals give smaller crops over a longer season.
Pick when fully red; strawberries don't ripen after picking.
Perfect for kids and small spaces: containers, baskets and window boxes.
Assorted varieties: check the tag for June-bearing vs. everbearing.

id_tips: Sprawling plant with hairy stems and divided, strongly scented leaves.
Small yellow star-shaped flowers in clusters.
Fruit varies by variety: cherry, grape, slicer, paste or heirloom, ripening red, pink, yellow, orange or purple.
Determinate (bush) types stop at a set height; indeterminate types keep growing and need tall support.

care.light: Full sun: 6+ hours of direct sun..
care.water: Water deeply and evenly; mulch to prevent cracking and blossom-end rot. Water at the base, not the leaves.
care.soil: Rich, well-drained soil with compost; add calcium (lime) if a soil test calls for it.

extra.label: Season
extra.text: Warm-season annual: plant after the last frost (mid-April or later in Atlanta). Stake or cage at planting (catalog: 3-4' tall, 24" spacing).

talk: America's favorite home-grown vegetable.
Cherry tomatoes are the easiest and most productive in Atlanta heat.
Plant deep: tomatoes root along the buried stem.
Assorted varieties: check the tag for type, size and whether it needs a tall stake.

id_tips: Multi-stemmed shrub with small, smooth, oval leaves.
Clusters of small white to pale pink urn-shaped (bell) flowers in spring.
Berries ripen from green to pink to dusty blue in early summer (catalog: Jn-Jl).
Brilliant red-orange fall color.

care.light: Full sun: 6+ hours of direct sun. Fewer berries in shade.
care.water: Keep evenly moist (shallow roots); mulch heavily with pine bark or straw.
care.soil: Must have acid soil (pH 4.5-5.5), rich in organic matter and well drained. Use azalea/blueberry fertilizer.

extra.label: Hardiness
extra.text: Rabbiteye and Southern highbush blueberries are well adapted to Atlanta. Plant two or more varieties for better pollination and bigger crops.

talk: Georgia is a top blueberry state: easy, long-lived and nearly pest-free here.
Plant at least two varieties that bloom at the same time for cross-pollination.
Doubles as a landscape shrub with spring flowers and great fall color.
Assorted varieties: check the tag for type (rabbiteye vs. highbush) and mature size (catalog: 3-10').
